subject.title: RFC: Skill routing metadata and evaluation hints for Harness-style OpenClaw setups

question: Should ClawHub standardize advisory routing and verification metadata for both skills and plugins, and should its first API expose only raw declarations or also produce ranked candidates?
rationale: The choice fixes a public manifest/API contract and determines whether self-declared safety information remains descriptive or becomes an input to trusted routing behavior.

options.title: Start with raw advisory metadata
options.body: Standardize a small versioned field set for intents, exclusions, and human-readable verification hints while deferring risk scoring and server-side ranking until provenance and evaluation rules are defined.

options.title: Adopt the full proposed contract
options.body: Include routing, risk, verification, playbook, and ranked-candidate behavior in one broader initial schema with corresponding anti-gaming and trust requirements.

options.title: Keep routing external
options.body: Continue exposing existing manifests and search APIs while requiring Harness-style systems to maintain their own routing and evaluation metadata.

recommendation.title: Start with raw advisory metadata
recommendation.body: Standardize a small versioned field set for intents, exclusions, and human-readable verification hints while deferring risk scoring and server-side ranking until provenance and evaluation rules are defined.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available history match for the existing structured skill metadata contract that the RFC would extend.
